name: Starter: Hawaiian
about: Hawaiian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Hawaiian order.

words.i: to, at; before what a verb acts on; before a verb: a done thing (ʻaʻole … i)
words.ka: the: ke before most words starting with k, e, a, o (and ke pākaukau); else ka
words.kaikuaʻana: older sibling of the same sex: a woman's older sister or a man's older brother
words.koʻu: my (o-class: bonds you don't control, hoa- friends, what holds or carries you)
words.ʻo: marks a name, or the one a sentence is about
words.kaʻu: my (a-class: what you control, get or make, bonds you cause; aʻu after ʻaʻohe)
words.iā: marks the one an action is for or to (iā ʻoe: you)
words.ana: going on, or will: after a verb, with e before it
words.ke: right now: before a verb, with nei after it
words.nei: now: after a verb, with ke before it

concept.line: A sentence usually starts with its action or description, then who or what it's about: Hele au i ke kula (go I to the school: I go to school), Liʻiliʻi ka hale (small the house: the house is small).
pehea is how, he aha what, i hea or ma hea where, and ʻehia how many or how much: Pehea ʻoe?

words.means: older sibling of the same sex: a woman's older sister or a man's older brother

concept.line: My is koʻu mainly for bonds you don't control and for what holds, clothes or carries you (koʻu makuahine: my mother, koʻu hoaloha: my friend, koʻu hale: my house), and kaʻu for what you control, get or make and bonds you cause (kaʻu kope: my coffee, kaʻu keiki: my child); your is kou or kāu.
The is ke before most words starting with k, e, a or o (ke kula, ke kai) and a few others (ke pākaukau: the table), and ka before most of the rest: ka hale (the house).

words.means: Hawaiʻi; Hawaiian (as a modifier, as in ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi, 'Hawaiian language')

concept.line: i says to or at (i ke kula: to the school) and comes before what many verbs act on (Inu au i ke kope: drink I the coffee), ma at or in (ma ka hale: at the house), mai from (mai Kaleponi mai: from California) and me with (me ka waiū: with milk).

words.means: particle used in e … ana to mark future or ongoing action

concept.line: he says a, and starts a sentence that says what something is: He kumu ʻo ia (a teacher she: she's a teacher), He hale nui (a big house).
